subject: Loading estimation issues among different SEM models

messages.author: 0e3ccb23145fa8dd
messages.subject: Loading estimation issues among different SEM models
parts:
Hi Lavaan community,

I am new to lavaan, and I am trying to fit some alternative SEM models using lavaan to test for the best fit for integration among characters. I am running into an issue trying to fit a model where there are two latent variables, and 6 characters from a 6 x 6 matrix. In model 1 the correlation between LV1 and LV2 is set to zero and in model 2 the correlation is freely estimated by the model, otherwise they are identical.

The problem I have is that in model 1 the respective first loadings per LV are constraint to 1, where I want them to be freely estimated by the model. This does happen correctly in model 2, and the only difference is that the correlation between LV1 and LV2 is freely estimable. I have pasted the model code and the sem function calls I use below. 

How can I specify the model so that all LV loadings are estimated freely whilst maintaining the correlation between LV1 and LV2 set to zero, with the LV's having a variance of 1?

Thanks in advance!

Model.1 <- "
LV1 =~ char1 + char2 + char3
LV2 =~ char4 + char5 + char6

char1~~a1*char1
char2~~a2*char2
char3~~a3*char3
char4~~a4*char4
char5~~a5*char5
char6~~a6*char6

LV1~~0*LV2

a1>0
a2>0
a3>0
a4>0
a5>0
a6>0
"

Model.2 <- "
LV1 =~ char1 + char2 + char3
LV2 =~ char4 + char5 + char6

char1~~a1*char1
char2~~a2*char2
char3~~a3*char3
char4~~a4*char4
char5~~a5*char5
char6~~a6*char6

LV1 ~~ a10*LV2

a1>0
a2>0
a3>0
a4>0
a5>0
a6>0
"

fit1 <- lavaan::sem(Model.1, sample.cov = matrix_6x6,
                    sample.nobs = nrow(df), std.lv = TRUE,)
summary(fit1)
semPaths(fit1)

fit2 <- lavaan::sem(Model.2, sample.cov = matrix_6x6,
                    sample.nobs = nrow(df), std.lv = TRUE)
summary(fit2)
semPaths(fit2)

Thank you for the fast reply Shu Fai!

For me it also works fine with the lavaan data example you provided. I refitted the models in a new session but that didn't change the outcome. So I simulated some random covariance and correlation matrices and used those to fit the model. For some matrices, the model estimated all the loadings and variances freely. However, for some it constrains one of the loadings for one or both of the LV's to one. Thus it seems it is highly variable based on the matrix structure whether the model can actually freely estimate the loadings. 

Ultimately, I want to estimate all the loadings freely, over multiple posterior iterations of my matrix. Is there a way to specify the model call to estimate all the loadings freely, or will this ultimately be determined by the matrix structure whether the model can freely estimate all the parameters I want?

All the best,
Corné

Hi Lavaan community,

I am new to lavaan, and I am trying to fit some alternative SEM models using lavaan to test for the best fit for integration among characters. I am running into an issue trying to fit a model where there are two latent variables, and 6 characters from a 6 x 6 matrix. In model 1 the correlation between LV1 and LV2 is set to zero and in model 2 the correlation is freely estimated by the model, otherwise they are identical.

The problem I have is that in model 1 the respective first loadings per LV are constraint to 1, where I want them to be freely estimated by the model. This does happen correctly in model 2, and the only difference is that the correlation between LV1 and LV2 is freely estimable. I have pasted the model code and the sem function calls I use below. 

How can I specify the model so that all LV loadings are estimated freely whilst maintaining the correlation between LV1 and LV2 set to zero, with the LV's having a variance of 1?

Thanks in advance!

Model.1 <- "
LV1 =~ char1 + char2 + char3
LV2 =~ char4 + char5 + char6

char1~~a1*char1
char2~~a2*char2
char3~~a3*char3
char4~~a4*char4
char5~~a5*char5
char6~~a6*char6

LV1~~0*LV2

a1>0
a2>0
a3>0
a4>0
a5>0
a6>0
"

Model.2 <- "
LV1 =~ char1 + char2 + char3
LV2 =~ char4 + char5 + char6

char1~~a1*char1
char2~~a2*char2
char3~~a3*char3
char4~~a4*char4
char5~~a5*char5
char6~~a6*char6

LV1 ~~ a10*LV2

a1>0
a2>0
a3>0
a4>0
a5>0
a6>0
"

fit1 <- lavaan::sem(Model.1, sample.cov = matrix_6x6,
                    sample.nobs = nrow(df), std.lv = TRUE,)
summary(fit1)
semPaths(fit1)

fit2 <- lavaan::sem(Model.2, sample.cov = matrix_6x6,
                    sample.nobs = nrow(df), std.lv = TRUE)
summary(fit2)
semPaths(fit2)

parts:
Hi,

I tried using the NA's to specify that the loadings should be estimated freely. It does not appear to make a difference, even if I specify all the loadings to be estimated freely with NA.  I have ran the code pasted below several times which generates a random correlation matrix that I used to fit the models with. Sometimes it estimates the loadings freely and sometimes it gets constraint to 1 or -1. So my worry is that the structure of the matrix determines whether all the loadings can be estimated freely. 

The data I used before I verifying this with the simulated data are based on median correlations from a posterior distribution, so perhaps it will be able to estimate the loadings better if they are fitted for every posterior iteration.

So I think the code itself isn't wrong, but it's mostly determined by the data used to fit the models. If anyone has further input on this I would love to hear it!

All the best,
Corné 

``` r
#===============================================================================
# Create cor & cov matrices:
library(Matrix)

# Total number of traits
N_traits <- 6

# Define variances for each trait
variances <- runif(N_traits, min = 0.1, max = 1)

# Create variance-covariance matrix
cor_matrix <- matrix(0, nrow = N_traits, ncol = N_traits)

# Number of correlations
n_cors <- (N_traits * (N_traits - 1)) / 2  

# Randomly generated correlation values
cor_values <- runif(n_cors, min = -0.9, max = 0.9)

# Populate the matrix with correlations
cor_matrix[upper.tri(cor_matrix)] <- cor_values
cor_matrix[lower.tri(cor_matrix)] <- t(cor_matrix)[lower.tri(cor_matrix)]
diag(cor_matrix) <- rep(1, N_traits)

# Ensure the correlation matrix is positive semi-definite
if (!all(eigen(cor_matrix)$values > 0)) {
  # Force the correlation matrix to be positive definite
  cor_matrix <- as.matrix(Matrix::nearPD(cor_matrix, corr = TRUE)$mat)
}

# Convert correlation matrix to a covariance matrix
std_devs <- sqrt(variances)
cov_matrix <- cor_matrix * (std_devs %o% std_devs)

# Ensure the covariance matrix is positive semi-definite
if (!all(eigen(cov_matrix)$values > 0)) {
  # Force the covariance matrix to be positive definite
  cov_matrix <- as.matrix(Matrix::nearPD(cov_matrix, corr = FALSE)$mat)
}

#===============================================================================
# SEM models

library(lavaan)

# Give matrix informative column & row names
row.names(cor_matrix) <- paste0("char", 1:6)
colnames(cor_matrix) <- paste0("char", 1:6)

Model.1 <- "
LV1 =~ char1 + char2 + char3
LV2 =~ char4 + char5 + char6

char1~~a1*char1
char2~~a2*char2
char3~~a3*char3
char4~~a4*char4
char5~~a5*char5
char6~~a6*char6

LV1~~0*LV2

a1>0
a2>0
a3>0
a4>0
a5>0
a6>0
"

Model.2 <- "
LV1 =~ char1 + char2 + char3
LV2 =~ char4 + char5 + char6

char1~~a1*char1
char2~~a2*char2
char3~~a3*char3
char4~~a4*char4
char5~~a5*char5
char6~~a6*char6

LV1 ~~ a10*LV2

a1>0
a2>0
a3>0
a4>0
a5>0
a6>0
"

Model.2alt <- "
LV1 =~ NA*char1 + NA*char2 + NA*char3
LV2 =~ NA*char4 + NA*char5 + NA*char6

char1~~a1*char1
char2~~a2*char2
char3~~a3*char3
char4~~a4*char4
char5~~a5*char5
char6~~a6*char6

LV1 ~~ a10*LV2

a1>0
a2>0
a3>0
a4>0
a5>0
a6>0
"

fit1 <- lavaan::sem(Model.1, sample.cov = cor_matrix,
                    sample.nobs = 4950, std.lv = TRUE)

fit2 <- lavaan::sem(Model.2, sample.cov = cor_matrix,
                    sample.nobs = 4950, std.lv = TRUE)

fit2alt <- lavaan::sem(Model.2alt, sample.cov = cor_matrix,
                    sample.nobs = 4950, std.lv = TRUE)

summary(fit1)
summary(fit2)
summary(fit2alt)
```

On Mon, Mar 24, 2025, 6:46 AM Corné de Groot <corned...@gmail.com> wrote:
Thank you for the fast reply Shu Fai!

For me it also works fine with the lavaan data example you provided. I refitted the models in a new session but that didn't change the outcome. So I simulated some random covariance and correlation matrices and used those to fit the model. For some matrices, the model estimated all the loadings and variances freely. However, for some it constrains one of the loadings for one or both of the LV's to one. Thus it seems it is highly variable based on the matrix structure whether the model can actually freely estimate the loadings. 

Ultimately, I want to estimate all the loadings freely, over multiple posterior iterations of my matrix. Is there a way to specify the model call to estimate all the loadings freely, or will this ultimately be determined by the matrix structure whether the model can freely estimate all the parameters I want?

All the best,
Corné
